about: The dimensions a learning-design decision and the evidence for it are described on, defined once. Three works named them separately: the evidence-axes coder (eval/evidence-axes/, L G C D O), the comparison record for interpreting an effect (methods/impact-evidence-comparison.md and observations' impact_context) and the principle-pattern affordances (principle-pattern-authoring.md). Each dimension says what it is called in each, so a page section, a coded cell and a benchmark check about the same thing use the same values. Read through scripts/evidence_dimensions.py. '?' means the text available does not say; it is never a default and never read as any other value.

dimensions.question: Who is learning, and from what observed starting point?

names.page_section: Learner state, objective and valued goal

expertise.novice: little or no prior knowledge of the target
expertise.mixed: spans levels, or results reported across levels

fields.learner_start: free text: the task-specific starting response or baseline, and whether arms were comparable

dimensions.note: age is developmental; population_band is the education system Kraft (2020) benchmarks against. A page asks for the observed starting response, not a label such as novice: the label is what a study reports, the response is what a design elicits.

dimensions.question: What capability is intended, on what kind of knowledge?

names.page_section: Learner state, objective and valued goal

knowledge_type.procedure: a step sequence to carry out
knowledge_type.principle: rules, causal models, explanations to be understood to be applied
knowledge_type.complex-skill: whole-task performance integrating several of the above
knowledge_type.attitude-motivation: interest, beliefs, self-efficacy as the target

element_interactivity.low: elements can be learned one at a time

dimensions.question: What does the learner want to accomplish, and why does it matter to them?

names.page_section: Learner state, objective and valued goal

fields.valued_goal: free text, elicited from the learner and kept apart from the designer's objective; agreement is an observation, not an assumption

dimensions.note: No coded evidence carries this yet: studies rarely report what learners valued. The axes coder does not code it, and the comparison record has no row for it.

dimensions.question: Under what conditions does the relationship hold?

setting.classroom: school or university class with a teacher
setting.online-instructor-led: digital with a live instructor or cohort

duration.days-weeks: several sessions over up to about two months

dimensions.question: What was changed, against what comparison, and what activity follows a response?

variable.example-problem-sequencing: order or pairing of examples and problems
variable.fading: gradually removing worked steps or support
variable.scaffolding: support adjusted to the learner, other than fading
variable.retrieval-practice: testing or recall practice versus restudy or none
variable.spacing: spaced or expanding versus massed schedule
variable.explicit-instruction: explicit or direct instruction versus discovery or implicit
variable.formative-assessment: assessment used to adjust teaching or learning
variable.problem-first: problem solving before instruction versus after
variable.case-comparison: comparing contrasting cases, solution methods, or correct and erroneous examples
variable.prompts: metacognitive, reflection or explanation prompts other than self-explanation of examples
variable.active-learning: active or peer-discussion formats versus lecture or passive study
variable.autonomy-support: choice and autonomy-supportive versus controlling conditions
variable.media-design: pictures, seductive details, multimedia presentation choices
variable.mastery-learning: mastery criteria with corrective loops versus fixed pacing
variable.learner-difference: NOT a design choice: a comparison between kinds of learners, kept so it is not lost
variable.other: none of the above; named in the treatment

dimensions.question: How were the conditions assigned, and so what kind of claim can the result support?

design.within-subject: each learner in every condition, counterbalanced
design.synthesis-experimental: meta-analysis or systematic review of experiments
design.synthesis-mixed: synthesis mixing experimental and non-experimental studies
design.argument: theoretical or narrative, no new data

assignment.credible-quasi-experiment: non-random, with a design that supports a causal reading

unit.homogeneous-synthesis: a pooled estimate over comparable studies
unit.heterogeneous-synthesis: a pooled estimate over unlike studies

dimensions.note: design is the coarse grain the axes coder reads from a text; assignment is the per-effect judgement a benchmark needs, and a non-random design needs a reader to say which of the two quasi-experimental values it is. Randomized and within-subject results, and syntheses of experiments, support do(D); the rest support an association.

dimensions.question: What was measured, with what instrument, and when?

outcome.delayed-retention: the same material after a day or more
outcome.learning-time: time or effort to reach a level
outcome.general-achievement: a course, unit or standardised test, or a pooled outcome that does not separate retention from transfer
outcome.assessment-accuracy: accuracy or validity of self-, peer- or teacher assessment

outcome_class.researcher-designed: a test built for the study

fields.measure_alignment: free text: how close the instrument is to the taught task
fields.score_range: free text: ceiling, floor or range restriction

dimensions.question: What was found, how big, how certain, and what does it not predict?

direction.+: better than the comparison (for time and load, less), significant or with an interval excluding zero
direction.0: no difference AND an equivalence test or adequate power is reported
direction.ns: no significant difference and no power or equivalence reported: inconclusive, never read as no effect
direction.?: the text does not show it

fields.standardization_denominator: free text: the SD the effect is scaled by

dimensions.question: Which explanations of a learner's response are live, and what observation would tell them apart?
dimensions.note: Design-side only: no study record carries it, which is why a page's diagnostic branches are proposals until learner responses test them.

evidence_status.known: at least one randomized, within-subject or synthesis-of-experiments result for these learners, goal and conditions
evidence_status.extrapolated: experimental results exist, for learners, goals or conditions that differ on at least one dimension or are not reported
evidence_status.associational: only correlational, qualitative or non-random evidence
